BANSHEE.name: Banshee
BANSHEE.description: Flying ground-attack harassment unit. Cloak and movement research improve access to exposed positions. It cannot fight aircraft and remains vulnerable to detection plus anti-air. Cloak's energy use limits concealed operating time.

BATTLECRUISER.name: Battlecruiser
BATTLECRUISER.acquisition: Starport + attached Tech Lab + Fusion Core.
BATTLECRUISER.description: Heavy aircraft with ground/air weapons, Tactical Jump, and researched Yamato Cannon. Durability and relocation enable distant pressure, but cost and tech create a substantial investment. Mechanical repair sustains it between fights. Jump is delayed relocation, not invulnerability; concentrated anti-air and control remain threats.

CYCLONE.name: Cyclone
CYCLONE.acquisition: Factory with an attached Tech Lab, as specified by the cached client tech_requirement.
CYCLONE.description: Mobile ground/air vehicle built around Lock On tracking damage. It rewards favorable distance and withdrawing from poor contact. Cached client tech requires an attached Factory Tech Lab. Other Cyclone designs differ substantially in production, cost, and Lock On behavior and should not be mixed into this baseline.

GHOST.name: Ghost
GHOST.acquisition: Barracks + attached Tech Lab + Ghost Academy.
GHOST.description: Specialist infantry with EMP, Steady Targeting, cloak research, and nuclear designation. EMP attacks shields/energy; Steady Targeting needs an eligible biological target and a completed channel. Energy, protected positioning, and detection determine spell value. It is not interchangeable with generic damage infantry.

HELLIONTANK.name: Hellbat
HELLIONTANK.acquisition: Factory + Armory; alternatively transform an existing Hellion with Armory tech.
HELLIONTANK.description: Short-range ground area attacker formed from Hellion or trained with Armory tech. Biological and Mechanical attributes permit biological healing and mechanical repair. It trades Hellion mobility for close fighting and suffers when kited before contact. It cannot attack aircraft.

HELLION.name: Hellion
HELLION.description: Fast ground vehicle using line splash, especially against Light targets. It supports scouting, worker pressure, and screening but needs room and favorable attack alignment. Armory tech permits transformation into Hellbat; this changes fighting role rather than creating a second unit.

LIBERATOR.name: Liberator
LIBERATOR.description: Aircraft with an anti-air weapon and a transformable ground-control mode. Air fire and the stationary ground firing zone are different roles. Repositioning or forcing combat outside the zone can remove useful ground damage.

LIBERATORAG.name: Liberator (Defender Mode)
LIBERATORAG.acquisition: Transform an existing unit or structure.
LIBERATORAG.description: Stationary mode attacking eligible ground units inside a selected firing zone. The circle restricts damage rather than providing ordinary all-direction ground fire. Enemies can bypass it or force redeployment; support must cover threats it cannot address in this mode.

MULE.name: MULE
MULE.acquisition: Orbital Command call-down; energy-based temporary summon.
MULE.description: Temporary worker called down by an Orbital Command using energy. It gathers minerals and can repair eligible targets, but does not establish a permanent worker economy or build the standard tech tree. Its limited lifetime and the Orbital's competing Scan expenditure affect the value of the call-down.

MARAUDER.name: Marauder
MARAUDER.description: Durable ground-only infantry specialized against Armored targets. Concussive Shells control eligible enemies, while Stimpack and Medivacs support mobility and fighting. It cannot cover aircraft, and its attribute bonus does not make it efficient against every ground composition.

MARINE.name: Marine
MARINE.description: Basic ranged infantry that attacks ground and air. Stimpack increases tempo at a health cost; Combat Shield increases durability. Healing and sufficient numbers improve sustained fighting, while splash and unfavorable range punish exposed groups. Its many small hits interact strongly with armor and infantry weapon upgrades.

MEDIVAC.name: Medivac
MEDIVAC.description: Flying transport and biological healer with energy and a speed boost. It supports eligible biological units but does not repair mechanical targets or provide detection. Cargo, healing energy, pickup space, and enemy anti-air constrain its practical value.

RAVEN.name: Raven
RAVEN.description: Flying detector and support caster without an ordinary attack. Auto-Turret supplies temporary damage, Interference Matrix disrupts eligible units, and Anti-Armor Missile supports allied fire. It needs energy and protection; a turret does not turn the Raven itself into a fighter.

REAPER.name: Reaper
REAPER.description: Mobile early scout and harassment infantry with cliff-jumping movement, a ground weapon, KD8 Charge, and out-of-combat recovery. It reaches information and worker lines inaccessible to ordinary infantry. Limited sustained army value and no anti-air make it an incomplete main-army core.

SCV.name: SCV
SCV.acquisition: Command Center; or Orbital Command; or Planetary Fortress.
SCV.description: Terran worker for minerals, gas, construction, and mechanical repair. Ordinary construction needs an assigned SCV throughout the work; another can resume an abandoned building. Repairing occupies the worker and spends resources, reducing current mining. Its ground attack is primarily an emergency rather than an army role.

SIEGETANK.name: Siege Tank
SIEGETANK.description: Mobile ground artillery that transforms into Siege Mode. Tank mode repositions and fights inside siege minimum range but lacks siege form's long-range area fire. It cannot attack aircraft and needs vision, screening, or favorable terrain to exploit artillery range.

SIEGETANKSIEGED.name: Siege Tank (sieged)
SIEGETANKSIEGED.acquisition: Transform an existing unit or structure.
SIEGETANKSIEGED.description: Stationary long-range ground artillery with splash and a minimum attack distance. Dense formations and controlled approaches are favorable targets. Surrounds, flanks, lack of vision, and air threats bypass its strongest conditions. Unsieging sacrifices the established firing position.

THOR.name: Thor
THOR.description: Large mechanical unit with a strong ground weapon and selectable anti-air role. It supplies heavy firepower but has a large footprint and limited mobility. Surrounds and control effects exploit those constraints. Choose anti-air mode for the enemy formation rather than assuming both air weapons fire together.

THORAP.name: Thor (High Impact Payload)
THORAP.acquisition: Transform an existing unit or structure.
THORAP.description: Thor mode emphasizing focused heavy-target anti-air rather than the alternate area-oriented air weapon. This transforms an existing Thor, not a new production order. Ground fighting and the unit's large movement footprint remain relevant in both modes.

VIKINGASSAULT.name: Viking (Assault Mode)
VIKINGASSAULT.acquisition: Transform an existing unit or structure.
VIKINGASSAULT.description: Landed Viking with a ground weapon and ground-unit vulnerabilities. Landing adds damage against suitable targets but removes fighter anti-air coverage. Transformation time and enemy proximity can make a return to flight unsafe.

VIKINGFIGHTER.name: Viking (Fighter Mode)
VIKINGFIGHTER.description: Mobile ranged anti-air aircraft. It pressures aircraft at range but cannot use its fighter weapon against ordinary ground targets. Landing trades flying movement and anti-air coverage for Assault Mode's ground weapon. Space and protection are needed to preserve its range advantage.

WIDOWMINE.name: Widow Mine
WIDOWMINE.description: Mobile state of a deployable burst-damage unit. It must burrow to arm its automated weapon rather than fight while moving. Placement, shot target, reload timing, and enemy detection determine its exchange value.

WIDOWMINEBURROWED.name: Widow Mine (burrowed)
WIDOWMINEBURROWED.acquisition: Transform an existing unit or structure.
WIDOWMINEBURROWED.description: Armed stationary form that shoots eligible ground or air targets. Shot splash can endanger nearby friendly units. Concealment between shots depends on the baseline's mine/Armory rules; burrow is not guaranteed permanent safety. Unburrow to relocate while the weapon is inactive.

ARMORY.name: Armory
ARMORY.description: Vehicle/ship upgrade building unlocked by Factory. It supplies Hellbat/Thor technology, higher infantry-upgrade access, and relevant mine/transformation interactions. Vehicle weapons, ship weapons, and shared plating remain different research families.

BARRACKS.name: Barracks
BARRACKS.description: Infantry producer and prerequisite for Factory, Bunker, Ghost Academy, and Orbital tech. Marines/Reapers need no Tech Lab; Marauders/Ghosts need an attached one, with Ghost Academy also required for Ghosts. Reactor capacity and Tech Lab access are alternative attachments. Lift/land can exchange add-ons.

BARRACKSREACTOR.name: Barracks Reactor
BARRACKSREACTOR.acquisition: Construct beside or connect to a grounded Barracks; mutually exclusive with a Tech Lab on that producer.
BARRACKSREACTOR.description: Parallel capacity for compatible basic Barracks products. It cannot supply the Tech Lab required by Marauders or Ghosts. Both production slots still need resources and supply; the Reactor is capacity rather than free units.

BARRACKSTECHLAB.name: Barracks Tech Lab
BARRACKSTECHLAB.acquisition: Construct beside or connect to a grounded Barracks; mutually exclusive with a Reactor on that producer.
BARRACKSTECHLAB.description: Local infantry add-on unlocking advanced products and hosting Stimpack, Combat Shield, and Concussive Shells research. Production requires an attachment to the actual Barracks; completed global research is a separate relationship. The add-on footprint needs usable access.

BUNKER.name: Bunker
BUNKER.description: Garrison defense whose damage comes from eligible occupants, not an independent normal gun. Position, repair access, and unload/retreat routes affect defense. Salvage can recover resources when the position is no longer useful.

COMMANDCENTER.name: Command Center
COMMANDCENTER.description: Town hall, collection point, SCV producer, and supply source. Lift/land allows relocation before committing an upgrade. Barracks unlocks Orbital Command; Engineering Bay unlocks the alternative Planetary Fortress. A flying base cannot collect resources or train workers normally.

ENGINEERINGBAY.name: Engineering Bay
ENGINEERINGBAY.description: Infantry and structure-upgrade building unlocking Missile Turret, Sensor Tower, and Planetary Fortress. Higher infantry upgrades additionally need Armory. The building itself provides no ordinary weapon or detection coverage.

FACTORY.name: Factory
FACTORY.description: Vehicle producer unlocked by Barracks. It opens Starport and Armory, while products have individual local Tech Lab and global Armory requirements. Position and add-on space affect usable capacity. A Tech Lab attached elsewhere does not unlock this Factory's advanced products.

FACTORYREACTOR.name: Factory Reactor
FACTORYREACTOR.acquisition: Construct beside or connect to a grounded Factory; mutually exclusive with a Tech Lab on that producer.
FACTORYREACTOR.description: Parallel capacity for Factory products without a Tech Lab requirement. It cannot replace the attachment needed by Tanks, Thors, or baseline Cyclones. Additional slots help only when compatible orders can be funded.

FACTORYTECHLAB.name: Factory Tech Lab
FACTORYTECHLAB.acquisition: Construct beside or connect to a grounded Factory; mutually exclusive with a Reactor on that producer.
FACTORYTECHLAB.description: Local vehicle add-on for Siege Tank, Thor, and the cached Cyclone, with vehicle-specific research. Armory remains an additional prerequisite for applicable products and research. An attached add-on and a completed global upgrade are different conditions.

FUSIONCORE.name: Fusion Core
FUSIONCORE.description: Starport-dependent advanced aircraft tech. Battlecruisers still need a Tech Lab on their producing Starport. The Core researches Yamato access and advanced support upgrades rather than producing aircraft itself.

GHOSTACADEMY.name: Ghost Academy
GHOSTACADEMY.description: Barracks-dependent Ghost technology/research building. Ghosts are trained at a Tech Lab Barracks. The Academy also prepares nuclear missiles; each is ammunition consumed by a successful strike rather than permanent global research.

MISSILETURRET.name: Missile Turret
MISSILETURRET.description: Engineering Bay-dependent detector and anti-air defense. It cannot attack ordinary ground attackers. Detection and weapon coverage are spatial, so one turret does not automatically protect an entire base.

ORBITALCOMMAND.name: Orbital Command
ORBITALCOMMAND.description: Command Center upgrade retaining SCV production and adding energy-based MULE, Scan, and Extra Supplies. These compete for the same energy. It can lift, unlike Planetary Fortress. The upgrade price is incremental to the already-owned Command Center.

PLANETARYFORTRESS.name: Planetary Fortress
PLANETARYFORTRESS.description: Defensive Command Center upgrade with ground attack and SCV production. It cannot lift and lacks Orbital MULE/Scan support. Repair workers improve durability but spend resources and mining time. Air threats require separate coverage.

REFINERY.name: Refinery
REFINERY.description: Gas structure built on a geyser. Assigned SCVs gather and return gas; the building alone produces no income. Worker counts, return distance, interruption, and the competing mineral requirement affect useful allocation.

SENSORTOWER.name: Sensor Tower
SENSORTOWER.description: Radar support giving advance warning of movement in its area. Radar contacts are not equivalent to direct vision or detection of a cloaked target. It has no ordinary weapon; information needs an army or defense that can respond.

STARPORT.name: Starport
STARPORT.description: Aircraft producer unlocked by Factory. Basic aircraft need no Tech Lab; advanced aircraft need an attached one. Fusion Core adds Battlecruiser tech on top of that local relationship. A lifted Starport cannot perform ordinary aircraft production.

STARPORTREACTOR.name: Starport Reactor
STARPORTREACTOR.acquisition: Construct beside or connect to a grounded Starport; mutually exclusive with a Tech Lab on that producer.
STARPORTREACTOR.description: Parallel production for compatible aircraft such as Viking, Medivac, and Liberator. It does not unlock Banshee, Raven, or Battlecruiser. Both active slots create resource and supply demand.

STARPORTTECHLAB.name: Starport Tech Lab
STARPORTTECHLAB.acquisition: Construct beside or connect to a grounded Starport; mutually exclusive with a Reactor on that producer.
STARPORTTECHLAB.description: Local aircraft add-on for Banshee, Raven, Battlecruiser, and relevant research. Battlecruiser also needs Fusion Core. Detaching removes this producer's advanced-product access even if a different Starport remains attached elsewhere.

SUPPLYDEPOT.name: Supply Depot
SUPPLYDEPOT.description: Supply structure and Barracks prerequisite. Raising blocks ground passage; lowering opens it while preserving supply and technology identity. Walls need access for friendly workers and units. Lost Depots can block production even when production facilities survive.

SUPPLYDEPOTLOWERED.name: Supply Depot (lowered)
SUPPLYDEPOTLOWERED.acquisition: Transform an existing unit or structure.
SUPPLYDEPOTLOWERED.description: Passable form of the same Depot, retaining supply and technology alias. Raising closes passage only when the action and local occupancy permit it. Lowering does not refund or rebuild the structure.

AUTOTURRET.name: Auto-Turret
AUTOTURRET.description: Temporary structure placed by Raven energy, attacking ground and air in range. It can be destroyed and expires. Placement legality and keeping the Raven safe are separate constraints; this is not a permanent SCV-built defense.

FLYING_PRODUCTION_BUILDINGS.name: Flying production buildings
FLYING_PRODUCTION_BUILDINGS.description: COMMANDCENTERFLYING, ORBITALCOMMANDFLYING, BARRACKSFLYING, FACTORYFLYING, and STARPORTFLYING are airborne states of existing structures. They cannot perform normal grounded production or use an attached add-on in flight. Landing needs legal space. A detached add-on does not fly with the main structure.

NUKE.name: Nuclear missile
NUKE.description: Single-use ammunition prepared at Ghost Academy and designated by a Ghost. Preparation, designation, and delayed impact are separate steps. It is not a permanent research upgrade or a strike that works without a surviving designator.
